blog.send-large-wedding-video.p_text.bef: Before diving into solutions, it helps to understand why your wedding video is such a hefty file. A professional wedding video shot in 4K resolution can easily reach 10-30GB for a full-length film, and even a 5-10 minute highlight reel can be 500MB-2GB.
blog.send-large-wedding-video.p_text.buy: Buy branded or decorative USB drives and include a printed label with your wedding date. It becomes a keepsake, not just a delivery method. Some couples even include a thank-you note with the drive.
blog.send-large-wedding-video.p_text.clo: Cloud storage is the most reliable way to share large wedding video files. Upload once, share a link, and let recipients download at their own pace.

Cloud storage is the safest method for international sharing. It avoids customs delays, shipping costs, and the risk of physical media being damaged in transit. Google Drive and Dropbox work in virtually every country with internet access.
blog.send-large-wedding-video.p_text.com: Compressing your wedding video to make it smaller inevitably reduces quality. Colors become less vivid, details get muddy, and fast-moving scenes (like dancing) show compression artifacts. For a once-in-a-lifetime video, this quality loss matters. The goal is to share the full-quality file, not a degraded version.
blog.send-large-wedding-video.p_text.cre: Create a simple page on your wedding website with embedded videos (Vimeo or YouTube) and download links. This gives family a single URL to visit for everything.
blog.send-large-wedding-video.p_text.ens: ensure your video looks great on every device, from a 65-inch TV to a smartphone screen.

blog.send-large-wedding-video.p_text.mos: Most email providers limit attachments to 25MB (Gmail) or 20MB (Outlook). A 25MB attachment is roughly 10-15 seconds of 4K video — not useful for sharing a wedding video. Use cloud storage or file transfer services instead.

Most wedding videographers deliver in MP4 (H.264 or H.265). This is universally playable. If you received a ProRes or MOV file, consider converting to MP4 for easier sharing — but do it once, from the original, using high-quality settings.
blog.send-large-wedding-video.p_text.no_: No. Google Drive stores and serves the exact file you upload without re-encoding it. The downloaded file will be identical to the original. YouTube and Vimeo do compress video, so use cloud storage if quality is your top priority.

blog.send-large-wedding-video.p_text.ope: Open the video file on your own device before sharing it. Make sure it plays completely, has audio, and looks correct. There's nothing worse than discovering the file was corrupted after your grandma spent three hours trying to download it.

blog.send-large-wedding-video.p_text.you: You've just received your finished wedding video and it's gorgeous. Now comes the challenge: how do you share a 2GB (or 10GB, or 20GB) video file with your parents, grandparents, and that aunt who lives across the country? Email attachment limits laugh at you. WhatsApp compresses your cinematic masterpiece into pixelated mush. And your grandma definitely isn't going to figure out a torrent link. Don't worry — there are several reliable ways to send large wedding video files without sacrificing the quality you paid for.

Your wedding video deserves to be seen — not stuck on a hard drive because the file is too large to send. Whether you choose cloud storage, file transfer services, or physical media, the methods in this guide will get your wedding video to every family member who wants to relive your special day.
